project.title: Constellation Framework
project.summary: A declarative framework for discovering, evaluating, and managing a software workspace through explicit package contracts and verified outcomes.

preview.description: Package facts, shared definitions, and relationships inform a request plan whose managed outcome is executed and verified.

blocks.body:
## Manage a connected workspace without losing package boundaries

My workspace combines desktop applications, command-line tools, AI services, and the integrations between them. Keeping that collection coherent requires more than a list of repositories: dependencies, installed commands, service state, source ownership, and validation all affect what can run.

I built Constellation Framework to describe those facts explicitly and manage the outcomes that depend on them. Packages provide their own intent and integration facts; shared definitions supply reusable behavior.

## Separate package facts from shared behavior

A manifest declares a package's identity, administrative state, worktree boundaries, capabilities, and relationships. The framework resolves those declarations against controlled definitions for services, environments, source updates, builds, installation, and publication.

That gives different package types a common management model while preserving their own runtimes and application data. A compatible improvement to shared behavior can reach its consumers without repeating the implementation in every package.

## Request an outcome, then verify its effects

A request identifies the work to pursue. Constellation resolves the relevant inputs, dependencies, handler, authority, validation, and recovery boundary before a managed change. Compatible prerequisite work can be shared, and sufficiently current evidence can satisfy a requirement without repeating execution.

Producing a build is distinct from installing it or activating a consumer. Each operation verifies the postcondition it claims, so a completed command can be understood in terms of what actually changed.

blocks.description: Discovery locates a package, evaluation records findings, and inspection follows the evidence for a saved result. RUN_ID stands for the returned evaluation identifier.

blocks.body:
## Make maintenance conclusions inspectable

Evaluation composes the applicable requirements for selected packages and records the conclusions with supporting evidence. Findings distinguish conformance problems, contextual constraints, and uncertainty. Their suggested responses help a maintainer choose the next action.

The project's evolution includes manifest-based discovery, independent package histories, declarative registry behavior, installed Python command boundaries, and fleet-wide ownership audits. Those milestones remain in the timeline while this overview describes the maintained management model.
